title: Big Mac Burger Bowl
subtitle: All the flavours of a Big Mac — lean beef, pickles, and a lightened-up special sauce — without the bun
steps: Mix Greek yoghurt, mustard, ketchup, pickle juice, vinegar, a pinch of garlic powder, and onion powder. Stir well and refrigerate while you cook.
Season the beef mince with garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Cook the mince in a non-stick pan over high heat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up as it browns. Drain any excess fat.
Add the cheddar slice over the hot mince and let it melt for 1 minute.
Build your bowl: start with a bed of shredded lettuce, then add the cheesy mince on top.
Top with diced tomato, onion, and pickles.
Drizzle the special sauce generously over everything.
Finish with a pinch of sesame seeds if using and serve immediately.
notes: Swap cheddar for dairy-free alternative if needed. Add rice for extra carbs.

seo.description: All the flavours of a Big Mac — lean beef, pickles, and a lightened-up special sauce — without the bun. 450 kcal, 45g protein. Ready in 15 minutes.

title: High Protein Cinnamon Rolls
subtitle: Fluffy Greek yoghurt buns with brown stevia & cinnamon filling, topped with a protein cream cheese frosting

ingredients.name: protein powder, unflavoured or vanilla — frosting

steps: Mix bread flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar alternative, and salt in a large bowl.
Add Greek yoghurt and stir until a soft dough forms. It will be slightly sticky — that's normal.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Roll the dough into a rectangle roughly 30×20 cm.
Melt 30g light butter and brush over the dough. Sprinkle with brown stevia and a generous dusting of cinnamon.
Roll the dough tightly from the long edge, then slice into equal buns.
Grease a baking dish with the 15g light butter and place buns inside, slightly apart.
Brush the tops with egg yolk for a golden finish.
Bake at 180°C / 375°F for 25–30 minutes until golden.
Make the frosting: beat together cream cheese, protein powder, vanilla extract, and sweetener. Add water slowly until it reaches a thick drip consistency.
Drizzle frosting over warm buns and serve.
notes: Per bun: 308 kcal | 20g protein | 39g carbs | 7g fat

title: Lemon Tiramisu
subtitle: Bright, creamy, no-bake lemon dessert layered with skyr and lemon curd

ingredients.name: sweetener of choice (sugar-free vanilla syrup used here)

steps: Stir the skyr with the sweetener and a bit of lemon zest until smooth.
Briefly dip two ladyfingers in milk and place them in a serving dish.
Spread half of the skyr cream on top of the ladyfingers.
Dip the remaining two ladyfingers in milk and place them on the cream layer.
Finish with the remaining skyr cream, spreading it evenly.
Top with zero-sugar lemon curd and chill well in the fridge before eating.

title: Cottage Cheese Pizza
subtitle: A crispy high-protein pizza base made from blended cottage cheese — all the flavour, none of the guilt
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Blend cottage cheese until completely smooth — no lumps.
Mix blended cottage cheese with eggs, oat flour, garlic powder, oregano, and salt until a thick batter forms.
Pour onto the baking tray and spread into a thin circle or rectangle, roughly 25cm across.
Bake the base for 20 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Remove from oven and spread with tomato sauce, then scatter mozzarella and pepperoni on top.
Return to oven for 5–8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Top with fresh basil or rocket and serve immediately.
notes: Blend the cottage cheese really well — lumps will stop the base from setting properly.

title: Oreo Protein Ice Cream
subtitle: Creamy Ninja Creami ice cream with Oreo chunks — built on a high-protein cottage cheese base
steps: Blend cottage cheese, protein powder, almond milk, sweetener, and vanilla until completely smooth.
Pour into your Ninja Creami pint container, leaving a small gap at the top.
Freeze for a minimum of 24 hours.
When ready, run the Ninja Creami on the 'Lite Ice Cream' or 'Ice Cream' setting.
Once processed, create a well in the centre with a spoon and add the broken Oreo pieces.
Run the 'Mix-In' setting once.
Serve immediately or refreeze for 30 minutes for a firmer texture.
notes: If the pint looks crumbly after the first spin, add a splash of milk and re-spin before adding the mix-in.

seo.description: Creamy Ninja Creami ice cream with Oreo chunks — built on a high-protein cottage cheese base. 290 kcal, 28g protein.

title: Cottage Cheese Cinnamon Rolls
subtitle: Soft, fluffy cinnamon rolls made with a high-protein cottage cheese dough — no yeast, no wait
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 375°F. Blend cottage cheese until completely smooth.
Mix blended cottage cheese with self-raising flour, sugar alternative, and salt until a soft dough forms. If too sticky, add flour a tablespoon at a time.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Roll into a rectangle roughly 30×20 cm.
Brush with melted light butter, then sprinkle evenly with brown stevia and cinnamon.
Roll tightly from the long edge and slice into equal buns.
Place in a greased baking dish, slightly apart, and bake for 25–30 minutes until golden.
Beat together cream cheese, protein powder, vanilla, and sweetener. Add water slowly until thick and drizzleable.
Pour frosting over warm rolls and serve.
notes: Blending the cottage cheese completely smooth is key — any lumps will show up in the dough.

title: Biscoff Protein Ice Cream
subtitle: Rich, caramelised Biscoff flavour in a creamy high-protein Ninja Creami — with a crushed cookie swirl
steps: Blend cottage cheese, protein powder, almond milk, Biscoff spread, sweetener, and vanilla until completely smooth.
Pour into your Ninja Creami pint container, leaving a small gap at the top.
Freeze for a minimum of 24 hours.
When ready, run the Ninja Creami on the 'Lite Ice Cream' or 'Ice Cream' setting.
Once processed, create a well in the centre with a spoon and add the crushed Biscoff cookies.
Run the 'Mix-In' setting once.

notes: Add an extra half tablespoon of Biscoff spread into the base for a stronger flavour. Re-spin if the texture looks crumbly after the first spin.

title: Cottage Cheese Queso Dip
subtitle: A creamy, high-protein queso made from blended cottage cheese and melty cheddar — no processed cheese block needed

ingredients.name: taco seasoning (or chilli powder + cumin + garlic powder)
milk, to loosen (add more if needed)
sliced jalapeño and chopped coriander, to garnish

steps: Blend the cottage cheese in a small blender or food processor until completely smooth and creamy.
Add the blended cottage cheese, shredded cheddar, salsa, and taco seasoning to a small saucepan over low-medium heat.
Stir constantly for 3–4 minutes until the cheese melts and the mixture turns smooth and glossy.
Add milk a splash at a time until the dip reaches your preferred consistency.
Taste and season with a pinch of salt if needed.
Transfer to a bowl, top with jalapeño and coriander if using, and serve warm with veggies, protein crisps, or low-carb tortilla chips.
notes: Reheats well — warm gently on the stove or microwave in 15-second bursts, stirring between each, if it firms up in the fridge.

subtitle: Fluffy, no-bake strawberry mousse blended with Greek yogurt and protein powder
steps: Dissolve the strawberry jelly mix in the boiling water and set aside to cool slightly.
Blend the yoghurt, jelly mixture, protein powder, and salt together until smooth.
Pour into a bowl and refrigerate for 3 hours until set.

title: High Protein Cinnamon Bread Sticks
subtitle: Soft blended oat bread swirled with cinnamon — just 190 kcal for the whole loaf
steps: Preheat the oven to 390°F (200°C).
Blend the oats, protein powder, egg white, water, stevia, and baking soda together until smooth, keeping the cinnamon aside.
Pour half the batter into a lightly lined loaf pan.
Sprinkle half the cinnamon on top and swirl it in with a knife.
Pour the remaining batter on top, sprinkle with the rest of the cinnamon, and swirl it in.
Bake for 12 minutes, then let rest before slicing and serving.
notes: Makes about 6 slices — roughly 32 kcal per slice if you cut it that way.
